newsitem.title: USA: Bargains among sluggish biotech stocks - Barron's. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT 2/12]
newsitem.headline: Bargains among sluggish biotech stocks - Barron's. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT 2/12]

text.p: Bargain-hunting investors can get good value for their money in the languishing biotechnology sector, Barron's quoted a California-based money manager as saying.

Michael Murphy, a money manager and newsletter editor in Half Moon Bay, Calif., said valuations in the sector were so low they have become "flat-out ridiculous," Barron's said in its December 2 edition.
Many biotechnology shares were trading at just two to three times cumulative research and development spending, compared to 10 times under normal circumstances, he said.

Murphy now recommended a 60 percent weighting in biotechs, and just 40 percent in technology shares, the newspaper said, with an emphasis on so-called second and third generation biotechnology companies.
Second generation biotechnology companies focus on using recombinant DNA technology to produce new drugs based on and often targeting human proteins, Barron's said.
Among these, the newspaper said Murphy liked COR Therapeutics, Amylin Pharmaceuticals, Cytel and NPS Pharmaceuticals.
He found third generation companies, which develop compounds that act within the cell rather than attacking proteins in the bloodstream, even more promising, Barron's said.
In this segment, he liked Vical, Sugen, Ribozyme Pharmaceuticals, Ligand Pharmaceuticals and Isis Pharmaceuticals, the paper said.

Barron's said the money manager also liked prospects for companies focused on discovering the functions of human genes rather than the drug development, like Human Genome Sciences and Sequana Therapeutics.
Murphy also recommended Chiron Corp, because it was substantially off highs, had a broad technology base and $500 million cash (Corrects from $500,000 cash).
